Northeastern Design System · Template · Sectionv0.1 · 2026-11-16

Section

The outer wrapper of every section pattern and the one owner of vertical rhythm. A page body is a run of sibling nu-section elements; each asks for the seam above it (--tight 64, standard 96, --chapter 128; one stop less under 960px) and the system gives exactly that much between the two sections' content, whatever their grounds. Hairlines are opt-in (--ruled). Styles: css/section.css, bundled after every component.

Template
Class

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
gaptight | standard | chapterstandard; chapter on its own ground or when ruledThe seam above the section, in total. Tight continues the section above; chapter changes the subject.
groundCanvas | data-mode="dark" | --sunkenthe page's groundA section on its own ground owns both of its seams and splits each evenly across its edge (64 inside, 64 outside at chapter).
ruledbooleanfalse--ruled: a hairline at the content width, midway in the seam above. Between two plain sections only.
flushboth | top | bottom | stacknoneThe section's content (a full-bleed picture or film) runs to that edge: no padding there, and the neighbour takes the whole gap. --flush-stack: both edges from 960px, the top only below.
bleedbooleanfalse--bleed: no inline padding; children place themselves with --layout-edge.
headingSectionHeadernoneAlways a SectionHeader variant (or the pattern's documented heading slot); what follows sits one --head-gap (48, 32 under 960px) below.
<main>
  <section class="nu-section">…</section>                       <!-- standard: 96 above -->
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--tight">…</section>      <!-- continues: 64 above -->
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--ruled">…</section>      <!-- chapter: 64, hairline, 64 -->
  <section class="nu-section" data-mode="dark">…</section>       <!-- Night: 64 outside + 64 inside -->
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--flush nu-section--bleed">…</section>   <!-- full-bleed picture -->
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--sunken nu-section--standard">…</section>   <!-- 48 + 48 -->
</main>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • A <section> names itself with aria-labelledby its heading; a section with no heading takes aria-label.
  • Night is data-mode="dark" on the section: every colour inside flips through the mode roles, so contrast holds on both grounds.

Usage

  • Leave block padding to the section: a pattern never sets padding-block or a block margin on its outer wrapper.
  • Use --tight for a section that continues the one above, --chapter once or twice a page.
  • Leave a section on its own ground at its default gap when its neighbour is flush: its inset there is half its gap, and 64 is the only half that is a token.
  • A hairline on every seam: --ruled marks a chapter.
  • Space a section with a spacer element, a top margin on its first child or a page stylesheet.
  • Put data-mode on a section whose ground is the page's.
Northeastern Design System · Template · Unit homev0.1 · 2026-11-16

Unit home

A unit site's front door in Persuade mode (Experiential Learning). The band plan: Night opens it (the bars and a display-size hero), Canvas states the unit in one line, one Night feature shows the six things that make it different, and Canvas carries the stories, figures, voices and the close. Two Night bands at most; the footers are chrome.

Experiential Learning at Northeastern University

Experience the world

As the world leader in experiential learning, Northeastern provides unparalleled opportunities to integrate classroom learning with global experiences.

Find your opportunity

Experiential learning is learning by doing.

Applying classroom knowledge to unique challenges at companies, research labs, and organizations around the world.

What is experiential learning?

What is experiential learning at Northeastern?

Every part of your journey at Northeastern is built for immersive learning, innovation, and integrating emerging technologies, like AI, to enhance creativity and career readiness.

  • Fully integrated from day 1

    Your immersive learning experience starts the day you arrive, evolving with you and enriching your degree from beginning to end.

  • Unmatched opportunities

    You’re in control of your journey with experiential options that span types, locations, and durations.

  • Learning without boundaries

    Study, work, and immerse yourself in culture, exploring new contexts and applying your academic knowledge.

  • Most expansive co‑op program

    Gain full-time professional work experience that positions you for a post-graduate job and a network for your future.

  • Excel at top companies

    A global network of 3,900+ employer partners, spanning industries and continents, for real-world problem solving with exceptional companies.

  • Dedicated support at every step

    Professional guidance from day 1 to post-graduation, helping you choose the right opportunities for your academic journey.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
band planslot → groundrequiredOpener Night · Statement Canvas · Feature Night · Stories Canvas · Figures Canvas · Voices Canvas · Close Canvas · Footer Night (chrome). Night is data-mode="dark" on the band; Canvas bands take the page ground. No third Night band: a page that wants a Closer gives up the feature.
headerHeaderStack --explore --over-mediarequiredFloats over the opener; the unit's bar sticks.
titlehidden h1 | HeroPage h1requiredThe unit's name. With HeroFrame the film's headline is an h2 under the hidden h1; with HeroPage --display the H1 is the hero's own, at display-xl.
openerHeroFrame | HeroPage --displayrequiredDisplay-size type either way (display-xl). Film when there is footage; a still with a phone focal point otherwise.
statementStatementrequiredThe unit in one line (two at most), its lead and one ArrowLink.
featureSectionHeader --split + __claims-gridnoneThe page's one Night feature: six claims as captioned square photos, 3×2 from 960px, 2×3 from 720px, a sideways strip on phones. Nothing links, so there is no card chrome: picture, h3 at h4 size, one sentence.
storiesStoryRailrequiredOn Canvas, after the feature; the newest story leads.
figuresStatBandnoneThree or four sourced figures and the sentence that frames them.
voicesVoices | RailVoicesPeople in their own words; Rail for a journey such as co-op.
closeActionBand --centerrequiredOn Canvas: the one red action the site exists for and one outline.
footerLocalFooter + GlobalFooterrequiredNight, as on every page.
<div class="nu-unit-home">
  <div class="nu-unit-home__top">
    <header class="nu-header-stack nu-header-stack--explore nu-header-stack--over-media" data-mode="dark">…</header>
    <h1 class="u-vh">Experiential Learning at Northeastern University</h1>
    <section class="nu-section nu-section--flush nu-section--bleed nu-hero-frame" data-mode="dark">…display-xl headline, lead, pill, pause…</section>   <!-- opener · Night -->
  </div>
  <div class="nu-section nu-unit-home__band nu-unit-home__statement"><div class="nu-statement">…</div></div>   <!-- Canvas -->
  <section class="nu-section nu-unit-home__band nu-unit-home__claims" data-mode="dark">              <!-- feature · Night -->
    <header class="nu-section-header nu-section-header--split">…h2…</header>
    <ul class="nu-unit-home__claims-grid" role="list" tabindex="0" aria-label="…">
      <li class="nu-unit-home__claim">
        <img class="nu-image nu-image--1x1" src="…" alt="…">
        <h3 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4">Fully integrated from day 1</h3>
        <p class="nu-text">Your immersive learning experience starts the day you arrive …</p>
      </li>
      …six…
    </ul>
  </section>
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--bleed nu-story-rail nu-unit-home__stories" data-dx-rail>…SectionHeader (h2, All stories), track, RailControls…</section>   <!-- Canvas -->
  <div class="nu-section nu-unit-home__band nu-unit-home__figures"><div class="nu-stat-band nu-stat-band--lead">…</div></div>
  <section class="nu-section nu-voices">…</section>
  <section class="nu-section nu-section--ruled nu-action-band nu-action-band--center nu-unit-home__close">…</section>
  <footer class="nu-local-footer" data-mode="dark">…</footer>
  <footer class="nu-global-footer" data-mode="dark">…</footer>
</div>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • One hidden h1; every band opens with an h2. One moving thing at a time, each with a pause.

Usage

  • Open on Night with display-size type, spend the one other Night band on the feature, and explain on Canvas, where the type steps down.
  • Two films or two StoryRails on one page.
  • Stat cards: the StatBand is type on hairlines.
  • A third Night band (a Closer after a Night feature).
  • The six claims as StoryCards with meta lines: they do not link, so they are not cards.
Northeastern Design System · Template · Section hubv0.1 · 2026-11-16

Section hub

The parent page of a section, shown as Experiential opportunities. The band plan: Night opens it (the bars, a tall HeroPage that stacks on phones, then the ContentsBar), a Statement starts the Canvas, Canvas chapters carry the doors and the featured cards, one Night feature (MediaText overlay) breaks the run, and Canvas closes it with the partners and an ActionBand. Two Night bands at most; chapters meet on one hairline, not on doubled padding.

Level
Template
Class
.nu-section-hub __top __band __statement __close
Composes
HeaderStack, HeroPage, ContentsBar, Statement, SectionHeader, ExpandingCards, CardGrid, ProgramCard, MediaText, LogoWall, ActionBand, LocalFooter, GlobalFooter
Used by
—
Found on

Find the right experiential opportunities for you.

Work at companies like Google through co-op, conduct research with faculty, study at one of the campuses in our global university system, or tackle community challenges, all while earning academic credit toward your degree.

Three ways in

Learn through your courses, through work, or beyond the classroom. Most students do all three before they graduate.

statementStatementnoneThe section in one line, its lead on columns 7–12.
doorsSectionHeader + ExpandingCards | CardGridrequiredThree to five ways into the section.

Northeastern Design System · Template · Campaign / competitionv0.1 · 2026-11-16

Campaign / competition

A time-boxed call, shown as the Next Up Founders Prize after applications closed. The band plan: Night opens it (the bars, a Night TitleCard --card carrying the campaign’s own mark, its status and its headline figure, the status Notice), Canvas lays out the rules of play (StatBand, who can enter, Steps with the current stage, key dates, a grouped FAQ), and an ActionBand closes on what a reader can do today. One status drives the page: the Notice, the Tag, the current Step and the current date all say the same thing.

  1. Global Entrepreneurship

Your first venture. Before your first semester.

High school founders pitch to founders and investors from Northeastern’s global entrepreneurship network, and get feedback to advance their ideas.

  • Applications closed
  • Finals November 17–20

Up to $100K

in cash prizes across finalists

Preparation
3–6 hours
Where
Submit from anywhere
Open to
High school students, grades 9–12

Applications for Next Up 2026 closed on September 30

The Reading Committee is reviewing every entry in the virtual semifinal round. Finalists will be notified in November.

Read the official rules

2,600+

ventures supported by Northeastern’s global entrepreneurship network

8,000+

mentorship matches

14

global campuses

$900M+

raised by IDEA venture accelerator

Who can enter

If you’re a high school student building something, you’re eligible. No connection to Northeastern is required.

Grade level
Any high school student over 13 years of age, grades 9–12
Team size
Solo, or with up to three teammates
Idea stage
Any stage counts, from a concept to a working prototype
School type
Public, private, charter or home-schooled
Geography
Open globally, in any field
Adult advisor
A teacher, counselor or mentor as your school contact

How it works

Applications for 2026 are closed. The Reading Committee is reviewing every entry.

  1. 1

    Complete the eligibility form

    Share your name, date of birth, country and parent or guardian contact information so we can confirm you’re eligible.

  2. 2

    Confirm your consent form

    Every entrant signs a consent form agreeing to the contest rules. If you’re under 18, it goes to your parent or guardian.

  3. 3

    Complete your application

    We email the full application: your school and contact details, the problem you’re solving, your idea and your AI angle.

  4. 4

    Submit your video pitch

    Upload a video pitching your idea with your written answers.

  5. 5

    Advance to the semifinals, then pitch in Boston

    The Reading Committee reviews every application in a virtual semifinal round. Finalists pitch on the Boston campus during Global Entrepreneurship Week.

What’s next for 2026

Semifinal timing depends on the Reading Committee’s availability.

  1. Mid-October

    Virtual semifinal review

  2. November

    Finalists notified

    Finalists hear directly; every applicant is told the outcome.

  3. Nov. 17–20

    Final pitch and Global Entrepreneurship Week celebration

    On the Boston campus. Additional details to follow.

Frequently asked questions

General

Can I still apply?

No. Applications for 2026 closed on September 30.

Format and logistics

What’s the date, time and location of the finale?

The finale takes place on the Boston campus in November.

How will I know if I’m a finalist?

Finalists are notified directly.

Judging and prizes

What are the prizes?

Up to $100K in cash prizes across finalists.

Can I appeal the judges’ decision?

No. All decisions of the judging panel are final.

Building something now?

Read the full rules for this year’s prize, or find a Northeastern entrepreneurship program that is open today.

Program / location

One place a program runs, read top to bottom: shown as N.U.in Greece, its hub and nine facet pages merged into one page of chapters. A TitleCard --margin carries the facts; a ContentsBar pinned under the HeaderStack jumps between chapters; each chapter uses the index layout (heading and strong rule in columns 1–6, content from column 7) so Prose, a DataTable, a Timeline, a DocumentList and the ContactBlocks share two edges.

N.U.in Greece

Your first semester at the American College of Thessaloniki, in a lively university town where one resident in ten is a student.

  • Fall 2026 location
  • Thessaloniki, Greece
Partner
American College of Thessaloniki (ACT)
Housing
Metropolitan or Capsis Hotel
Arrival
Sept. 12–13
Departure
Dec. 12–13
  • Courses at N.U.in Greece

On this page

  1. Location
  2. Academics
  3. Housing
  4. Important dates
  5. Preparing for departure
  6. Documents
  7. Contact

Location

Thessaloniki and the neighborhood around the residences.

Thessaloniki is the second largest city in Greece and a gateway to Southeastern Europe. Founded in 315 B.C., it is now a modern seaport of over one million people, known for its wide avenues, neoclassical buildings, Byzantine monuments and warm hospitality.

Neighborhood: the hotel residences are within walking distance of the boardwalk and downtown. A short stroll takes you to the White Tower and Aristotle Square, with views of Mount Olympus across the bay.

Thessaloniki, fall semester

MonthAverage lowAverage highPrecipitation
September59°F81°F0.79 in
October52°F70°F1.97 in
November45°F57°F3.15 in
December37°F50°F1.97 in

Academics

The partner institution and how courses work.

The American College of Thessaloniki is an American-accredited college just outside the city center, offering degrees across the arts and sciences. Its campus is framed around Bissell Library, one of the largest university libraries in Southeast Europe.

  • Class schedule. You receive your finalized schedule during on-site orientation in Thessaloniki.
  • Textbooks. Wait until you are on site; many are digital or in Bissell Library.
  • Grading scale. Set out in the location’s academic handbook, published at pre-departure orientation.

Housing

Required for the length of the program.

N.U.in Greece students live in the Metropolitan or Capsis Hotels. ACT runs daily private buses between each hotel and campus on weekdays, about 30–45 minutes each way.

Amenities: each room is shared by two students, with a private bathroom, linens, towels, a small refrigerator, air conditioning and wireless internet.

Meals: breakfast and dinner daily in the hotel dining room. N.U.in staff work with the hotel on any dietary restrictions.

Important dates

Program dates are subject to change.

  1. Sept. 12–13

    Student arrival days

    Group flight students arrive together; transportation to the residence is included.

  2. Sept. 14–20

    On-site orientation

  3. Sept. 21

    First day of classes

  4. Oct. 24–28

    Fall break

    No classes.

  5. Dec. 4

    Last day of classes

  6. Dec. 12–13

    Student departure days

Preparing for departure

Orientation, packing and the group flight.

The N.U.in Program hosts Pre-Departure Orientation in the summer before you leave. For a suggested packing list, read the N.U.in packing guide (PDF).

Adapters and voltage converters: the electricity supply in Greece runs at 220–240 volts and 50 hertz. Check your devices before you bring them.

Group flight: the program fee includes a group flight to and from Greece, with transportation between the airport and your residence. Registration opens in late spring through Application Status Check.

Documents

Read the handbook before you choose courses.

  • N.U.in Greece academic handbookPDF · Fall 2026
  • Program modification request formPDF · Updated July 2026
  • N.U.in supplemental guide to participant conductPDF · 2026

Reach The N.U.in Program and the Global Experience Office through ServiceNow, which also answers common questions about GEO programs.

300 Mass Ave. Launch Week

Two days of curated conversations, a showcase of founders from across Northeastern’s global university system, facilitated networking and the hackathon finals.

  • Entrepreneurship
  • Boston
Nov17–18Tue–Wed
  • 9 a.m.–6 p.m. ET
  • 300 Massachusetts Avenue, Boston
Register on Cvent

About

Launch Week opens Northeastern’s 300 Startup Hub to founders, students, mentors and investors. Drop in any time; advance registration is required for select sessions.

Both days run an interactive showcase of global entrepreneurship at Northeastern: ventures, products and ideas from founders across the university’s global network.

Agenda

Tuesday, November 17

  1. 9–10 a.m.

    Brewing connections

    Casual conversation over coffee for anyone in the Northeastern community.

  2. 10 a.m.

    From lab to launch: commercialization broken down

    Curated conversation
    • Shashi Murthy, founder and vice provost for global innovation, Northeastern University
    • Raymond Fu, COE Distinguished Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering and Khoury College of Computer Sciences
  3. 3:30 p.m.

    Leaders @300: It’s never been easier to start a company, and never been harder to scale one

    Featured event

    A conversation with Brian Halligan, co-founder of HubSpot and senior advisor at Sequoia Capital, on building and scaling a marketing movement.

Wednesday, November 18

  1. 9–11 a.m.

    300 Connect: Live

    Facilitated networking for founders and mentors, hosted by Misneach and the McCarthy(s) Venture Mentoring Network.

  2. 4:30 p.m.

    Hackathon finals

    62 hours. 40 builders. One building. Co-hosted with SCION.

Speakers

  • Brian Halligan

    Co-founder of HubSpot; senior advisor, Sequoia Capital

  • Shashi Murthy

    Founder and vice provost for global innovation

    Northeastern University

  • Raymond Fu

    COE Distinguished Professor

    Electrical and Computer Engineering; Khoury College

  • Nikko Lara

    Co-founder and COO, Otto AI

    D’Amore-McKim School of Business, 2015

300 Massachusetts Avenue

Launch Week runs at the 300 Startup Hub, Northeastern’s workspace for founders in Boston. The hub’s page has parking, transit and accessibility details.

  • None. Presentational only.

Detail with section nav

The reading page inside a section: the university and unit headers, a TitleCard --margin with the Breadcrumb and the page's facts in its margin column, then the section's pages in a sticky SectionNav (three columns) beside one reading column (columns five to twelve) that carries Prose, a DataTable, a DocumentList, an Accordion and, last, the ContactBlock. The reading column starts on column five, the same line the index organisms and the LocalFooter use, so every band below the hero shares one left edge. Replaces nuin's 77 facet pages and research policy pages.

Academics

Your semester at the American College of Thessaloniki: the partner institution, the support you can reach abroad, and how accommodations work.

Partner
American College of Thessaloniki (ACT)

N.U.in Greece

  • Location
  • Academics
  • Housing

Partner institution

As its name suggests, the American College of Thessaloniki is an American-style institution just outside the city center of Thessaloniki, accredited in the United States and offering degrees across the arts and sciences. The campus is framed around Bissell Library, one of the largest university libraries in Southeast Europe, and the Stavros S. Niarchos Technology Center.

Class schedule
Course offerings are subject to change. You receive your final schedule at on-site orientation in Thessaloniki.
Textbooks
ACT offers many textbooks digitally and in print at Bissell Library. Wait until you are on-site, so you can check each syllabus first.
Grading scale
How ACT grades convert to Northeastern grades is set out in your location’s academic handbook, below.

Courses at N.U.in Greece

First 5 of 33 courses

NU course equivalent NUpath NU credits
ANTH 349Intercultural Communication in Theory and PracticeCOMM 2303Intercultural and Global CommunicationSI, DD4.00
ARCH 120Architecture in Greece through the AgesARCH 2370Topics in Architectural HistoryWI4.00
ART 121Greek Art through the AgesARTH 1990Art History ElectiveNone4.00
CS 180Discrete StructuresCS 1800/1802Discrete Structures + SeminarFQ5.00
ECON 102Introductory MicroeconomicsECON 1116Principles of MicroeconomicsSI, AD4.00

Course offerings are subject to change. See all 33 courses in the N.U.in curriculum

Academic resources abroad

Tutoring and extra support are open to every student. ACT faculty, staff and peers are ready to help.

  • Bissell Library. Reference librarians, study space for individuals and groups, and the Learning Hub, where you can walk in or book a tutor or writing support.
  • Faculty support. ACT professors offer extra help during the weekly office hours listed in each syllabus.
  • Northeastern Peer Tutoring on Knack. Free peer tutoring for every Northeastern undergraduate. Search by the NU equivalent course title or code; questions go to peertutoring@northeastern.edu.

Learning disabilities

If you need accommodations in N.U.in Greece, apply through Northeastern’s Disability Access Services, which works with the partner institution on each request. Speak to your professors individually as well, so they know about any approved accommodations.

Handbooks and forms

Read your location’s handbook before you choose courses.

  • N.U.in Greece academic handbookPDF · Fall 2026
  • Program modification request formPDF · Updated July 2026
  • Study abroad academic resource guidePDF

Course selection questions

How will the courses appear on my transcript?

Your N.U.in courses and letter grades appear directly on your Northeastern transcript and count toward your GPA.

Why are some or most of my classes already selected for me?

Many first-year programs of study have a prescribed curriculum.

Once I choose my courses, are my selections final?

No. You’ll adjust them with your home college advising office from mid-June through July.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headerGlobalHeader + HeaderStackrequiredGlobalHeader solid, current set to the university section the unit lives in. HeaderStack with the unit's SiteIdentity and the section that holds the page marked current.
heroTitleCard --marginrequiredBreadcrumb from the site home to the page, the H1 (at most 30 characters), a one-sentence lead, and up to four facts (KeyValue --inline) in the margin column.
navSectionNavrequiredThe section's pages with this one current. Rendered twice by the template: a sticky rail from 960px, a disclosure above the content below it.
mainProse, DataTable, DocumentList, AccordionProseThe reading column, in the editor's order. Prose for running text; the others only when the page has rows, files or questions.
contactContactBlocknoneAlways last in the column: who answers questions about this page.
footerLocalFooter + GlobalFooterrequiredThe unit's footer on the page's ground, then the university's on Night.
<div class="nu-detail">
  <header class="nu-global-header" data-mode="dark">…</header>
  <header class="nu-local-header">…</header>
  <section class="nu-section nu-title-card nu-title-card--margin">…breadcrumb; __main: h1, lead; __aside: KeyValue facts…</section>
  <div class="nu-detail__body">
    <details class="nu-section-nav__disclosure nu-detail__disclosure">…phones…</details>
    <div class="nu-detail__nav"><nav class="nu-section-nav" aria-label="N.U.in Greece">…</nav></div>
    <div class="nu-detail__main">
      <div class="nu-prose">…</div>
      <div class="nu-data-table nu-data-table--compact">…</div>
      <section class="nu-document-list">…</section>
      <section class="nu-accordion">…</section>
      <section class="nu-contact-block">…</section>
    </div>
  </div>
  <footer class="nu-local-footer">…</footer>
  <footer class="nu-global-footer" data-mode="dark">…</footer>
</div>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • One h1 (the TitleCard). The SectionNav title and every organism heading inside the column are h2, set at h3 or h4 size so the outline stays flat while the type steps down.
  • On phones the SectionNav disclosure comes first in source after the hero, so the section's pages are reachable before the content; from 960px the rail is a nav landmark beside it.
  • The sticky rail never traps focus: it is a list of links, and it stops sticking where the column ends.

Usage

  • Keep the reading column at one left edge: Prose, tables, files, questions and contact all start on column five.
  • Let organisms inside the column use their own index layout (label left, rows right) once the column passes 960px of viewport.
  • End the column with the ContactBlock, even when the contact copy repeats across a section's pages.
  • A coloured sidebar, or a sidebar of cards with icons (nuin's red panel).
  • Put the section's pages in the HeaderStack as well: the header names the section, the rail lists its pages.
  • Run Prose past 68ch to fill the column; the space to its right is the page's margin.
Northeastern Design System · Template · Finder pagev0.1 · 2026-11-16

Finder page

The directory page: the headers, a TitleCard --margin that names what is being browsed, a Notice that says where the listing's data comes from, then the Finder organism (FilterPanel rail, ListToolbar, results, Load more or Pagination) and the footers. The Notice sits on the Finder's own 3 : 9 split, over the results column, so the caveat reads with the count it qualifies. Replaces experiential opportunities, GEO Browse Programs, research institutes and staff directories.

Our people

Alessandro Vespignani

Executive director of the Network Science Institute; Sternberg Family Distinguished University Professor

  • College of Science
  • Khoury College of Computer Sciences
  • Bouvé College of Health Sciences
Next profile: James Monaghan

Research areas

  • Network science
  • Techno-social systems
  • Contagion processes
  • Emerging diseases
  • Information and social networks

Biography

Alessandro Vespignani is the Sternberg Family Distinguished University Professor at Northeastern University, with joint appointments in the College of Science, the Khoury College of Computer Sciences and the Bouvé College of Health Sciences. He is the executive director of the Network Science Institute.

His research studies “techno-social” systems, where infrastructures made of different technological layers interoperate with the social component that drives their use and development. The aim is to understand how the same elements, assembled in large numbers, can give rise to different large-scale behaviors, opening the way to quantitative computational approaches and forecasting.

His main lines of research are:

  • Analytical and computational models for the co-evolution and interdependence of large-scale social, technological and biological networks
  • Contagion processes in structured populations
  • Predictive computational tools for the spatial spread of emerging diseases
  • The dynamics and evolution of information and social networks

Vespignani received his undergraduate degree and PhD, both in physics, from the University of Rome La Sapienza.

Network Science Institute

Studies the networks behind epidemics, economies and the brain, from the physics of complex systems to the data science that predicts how they spread.

Role
Executive director

Story

Research news

From social media to body image and back: Rachel Rodgers reveals the complexity of a two-way relationship

How someone feels about their body shapes how they use social media, and what the algorithm shows them shapes how they feel. The APPEAR Lab is measuring both directions.

  • By Kiran Johnson
  • February 14, 2025

Share this story

A teenager opens their phone and is met with posts of people with defined arms and sculpted abs, then exercise gadgets and metabolism-boosting drinks. Afterward, they spend some time looking in the mirror: I should go to the gym, they think. I should start a new diet.

Rachel Rodgers, associate professor in the Department of Applied Psychology, directs the Applied Psychology Program in Appearance and Eating Research (APPEAR) Lab. She works to characterize the relationship between social media use and body image, which means refining the tools that measure what social media does to the people who use it.

The way someone feels about their body on a given day shapes how they use social media: how long they hover over a post, whether they watch a full video, whether they follow a profile. Those choices shape what the algorithm shows them next, and over and over, the cycle repeats.

“Before deciding how we intervene, I think we really need to understand it all.”

Rachel Rodgers, associate professor of applied psychology

In a 2023 study published in Computers in Human Behavior, the APPEAR Lab and Australian colleagues followed a large sample of adolescents from schools in Melbourne over a year. Membership in the higher social-media-use subgroups was linked to greater body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint and muscle-building behaviors.

“In terms of body image and eating disorder risk, time is not the index that is most highly associated,” Rodgers says. “It’s more how much time you’re spending engaging in photo-related activities on social media.”

Body image and identity

The research fits into Rodgers’ larger focus on how appearance serves economic and political goals. The “trending” appearance, she says, is usually one that only people with the social and financial resources to pursue it can reach.

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headerArticleHeaderrequiredSection link or Breadcrumb; headline as H1 (sentence case, no length limit beyond two lines at 1440); deck; byline and date; ShareLinks; lead Figure optional.
bodyProse --lgrequiredParagraphs and H2 subheads from the CMS; pull quotes arrive as CMS blockquote + cite, which Prose sets in Quote's pull form; Figure molecules sit between paragraphs when the story has photographs (this one has none of record).
relatedCardGrid of StoryCardsnoneThree stories from the same section, with an ArrowLink to the section.
prefooterActionBandsitewideThe university's Take action band, Night.
<div class="nu-story">
  <header class="nu-global-header" data-mode="dark">…</header>
  <div class="nu-story__head"><header class="nu-article-header">…</header></div>
  <div class="nu-story__body"><div class="nu-prose nu-prose--lg">…<blockquote>…<cite>…</cite></blockquote>…</div></div>
  <div class="nu-story__related"><section class="nu-card-grid">…</section></div>
  <section class="nu-action-band" data-mode="dark">…</section>
  <footer class="nu-global-footer" data-mode="dark">…</footer>
</div>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • The headline is the page's only h1 (the source sets it as an h2). Subheads inside the body are h2.
  • A pull Quote repeats words from the body: mark it aria-hidden only if it duplicates a sentence word for word; a quote that appears only in the pull stays readable.
  • Every inline Figure has alt text written for the story; the caption is not the alt.

Usage

  • Keep the body on the headline's left edge; let the right margin breathe.
  • Put the byline and date under the deck, on the meta row, never as an eyebrow above the headline.
  • Run the body the full 12 columns.
  • A related grid of more than three, or a carousel of them, before the ActionBand.
Northeastern Design System · Template · Form pagev0.1 · 2026-11-16

Form page

A contact or inquiry page: a TitleCard --margin that says who will answer and how fast, the Form organism in columns 1–7 beside a sticky ContactBlock in columns 9–12 (for people who would rather write or call someone directly), and an Accordion of routing questions that sends specialist requests to the right office before they reach the form. Replaces research Connect with us, experiential employer inquiry and entrepreneurship contact pages.

contactContactBlockrequiredThe offices and people behind the form, as people rows. Sticks beside the form from 960px; follows it below.
faqAccordionnoneQuestions that route a request elsewhere. Grouped, so its heading takes columns 1–6 and the questions run on column 7.
<div class="nu-form-page">
  <header class="nu-global-header" data-mode="dark">…</header>
  <section class="nu-section nu-title-card nu-title-card--margin">…breadcrumb; __main: h1, lead…</section>
  <div class="nu-form-page__body">
    <div class="nu-form-page__form"><form class="nu-form">…</form></div>

</div>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • One h1 (TitleCard); the ContactBlock and Accordion headings are h2.
  • The Form's error summary takes focus on a failed submit; the sticky ContactBlock must never cover it (it sits beside, never over, the form).
  • Required fields say (required) in the label, not only an asterisk.

Usage

  • Say how long a reply takes, in the hero and again beside the submit button.
  • Mark required fields; the research form marks none.
  • A 20-row directory above the form (the visitor scrolls past the people to reach the box).
  • Hidden anti-spam fields with visible labels.
Northeastern Design System · Template · Leadershipv0.1 · 2026-11-16

Leadership

The people who run something, in three tiers: a TitleCard --margin, the one leader who heads the list as a FeaturedPerson band on Night, the leadership index as FeaturedPerson rows on Canvas (alternating sides, two pills each), and the wider roster as a CardGrid of PersonCards. The roster is shown in its real no-photo state, the trustees emeritae, whose records carry a name and no portrait: the PersonCard glyph holds the frame so the grid keeps its rhythm. Replaces www senior leadership, office pages and board rosters (28–72 people).

Northeastern Design System · Template · Policyv0.1 · 2026-11-16

Policy

A long reference document: a TitleCard --margin whose meta line (a MetaList) says what the page is, who owns it and when it last changed, then a sticky TableOfContents (columns 1–3) beside the document in Prose (columns 5–12), and the owner's ContactBlock on the same reading edge. On phones the contents fold into a disclosure pinned under the header that names the section being read. Built for the www privacy policy (about 21,000px, fourteen numbered sections and no contents today); shown here as an excerpt of its first sections.

Welcome

Northeastern University and its subsidiaries and affiliates are committed to protecting the privacy of the personal information we collect when providing undergraduate, graduate and continuing education programs; through our central websites, www.northeastern.edu and neu.edu, and our mobile apps; and in support of our marketing, fundraising, IT and other internal operations.

Northeastern has four core privacy policies:

  • The general Privacy Policy, covering personal information collected through our sites and apps and in support of our operations. Its terms are below.
  • The Policy on Privacy for Students, Applicants, and Alumni.
  • The Policy on Privacy for Employees, Job Applicants, Contractors, and Others Working with the University.
  • The Policy on Privacy in Research, covering the personal information of research subjects.

I. General privacy policy scope

This general Privacy Policy describes how Northeastern collects and handles personal information through your use of our sites and apps and in support of our operations. It also describes your privacy rights and choices, and our practices when processing personal information for these purposes.

For more information about this Privacy Policy and your rights under applicable law, contact us at privacy@northeastern.edu.

II. What information do we collect?

We collect personal information that you give us when you visit the sites or apps, or when we engage with you through our operations, such as marketing, fundraising and IT. This information includes:

  • Name, title, age and date of birth
  • Contact information, including address, email address and telephone numbers
  • Attendance at Northeastern University events
  • Records of communications between you and the University

Automatically collected data

When you use the sites and apps, information including the following may be created and automatically logged in our systems.

Sections III to XIV continue in the full policy: how we use, share and retain information; cookies; security; individual rights; and children under 13.

Last updated on April 24, 2026

Questions or complaints

To ask about your personal information, or to access or remove it, write to the Chief Privacy Officer.

  • Chief Privacy Officer

    Northeastern University, 716 Columbus Avenue, Suite 301, Boston, MA 02115

    privacy@northeastern.edu

  • Data Protection Officer

    Northeastern University London, Devon House, 58 St. Katharine’s Way, London E1W 1LP

    dpo@nulondon.ac.uk

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
heroTitleCard --marginrequiredH1 (at most 30 characters), a one-sentence lead, and an inline MetaList as its __meta line: document type, owner, Updated with a time.
tocTableOfContentsrequired for more than four sectionsBuilt from the document's H2s (and H3s under the current one), with the document's own numbering. The template renders the rail from 960px and the disclosure below.
documentProserequiredThe policy text. Sections are h2 with the document's numbering in the text; subsections h3. Ends with Prose's Last updated line.
contactContactBlockrequiredThe office that owns the policy and how to exercise rights under it.
prefooterActionBandsitewideAs on every www page.
<div class="nu-policy">
  <header class="nu-global-header" data-mode="dark">…</header>
  <section class="nu-section nu-title-card nu-title-card--margin">…h1, lead, <ul class="nu-meta-list nu-meta-list--inline nu-title-card__meta">…Updated <time>…</time></ul>…</section>
  <nav class="nu-table-of-contents nu-table-of-contents--disclosure nu-policy__disclosure">…phones…</nav>
  <div class="nu-policy__body">
    <div class="nu-policy__toc"><nav class="nu-table-of-contents" aria-labelledby="toc-title">…</nav></div>
    <div class="nu-policy__main">
      <div class="nu-prose">…</div>
      <section class="nu-contact-block">…</section>
    </div>
  </div>
  <section class="nu-action-band" data-mode="dark">…</section>
  <footer class="nu-global-footer" data-mode="dark">…</footer>
</div>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • The contents is a nav with its own visible title; the current section carries aria-current="location", updated as the reader scrolls.
  • Section headings keep their Roman numerals in the text so the contents, the headings and any printed copy agree.
  • The phone disclosure is a native details; it names the current section in its summary so a screen-reader user hears where they are.

Usage

  • Show the last-updated date twice: in the hero meta and at the foot of the document.
  • Keep the document at 68ch; the right side of the reading column stays empty on purpose.
  • A 21,000px page with no contents.
  • Uppercase or letter-spaced section labels; the numbering carries the order.
